analysis:
Market is in a confirmed uptrend (SPY +1.2% vs SMA50, slope +3.94%), which justifies staying long but not aggressively chasing. Portfolio is 79% deployed with four open positions, all in the green: LII (+3.56%), AMP (+8.77%), CI (+2.09%), A (+0.76%). None show thesis breaks — all remain above entry with intact fundamentals. AMP in particular has appreciated nicely and should be monitored for a trailing-stop raise to protect gains. LII is the largest position (~28% of equity) and is close to the 25% hard cap; no additions there.

The concerning signal is the track record: 22.2% win rate, profit factor 0.66x, Sortino -4.89, and the last five closed trades were all stops. This pattern demands extreme selectivity — no trades unless the setup is genuinely asymmetric. Available headroom for new buys is only $15,976, which further constrains sizing.

Of the 30 screened candidates, most fail on at least one of: (1) too extended from SMA200 (MU +120%, MRVL +100%, FLEX +68%, AMAT +78%, CSCO +33%), (2) range position above 80% (HWM at 89%), (3) earnings within 2 weeks introducing binary risk (CTAS July 15, COF July 21, MRSH July 21, NOW July 22, FLEX July 22, NVR July 22, BX July 23, ALLE July 23), or (4) weak fundamentals relative to valuation.

FDS (FactSet Research Systems) stands out as the single genuine asymmetric setup: high-quality subscription financial data business with 30%+ operating margins, 27% ROE, ~7% FCF yield, and a PEG of 1.19 after a significant drawdown from $442 to $250 (24% of 52w range). The stock has re-entered a confirming uptrend from the lower half of its range, with earnings not until September 17 (73 days), giving clear runway. Sizing is constrained by the $15,976 headroom cap. One trade only; cash remains the dominant position at ~21% plus the headroom reserve.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $250 or better; accept fills up to $252 on market open strength. Do not chase above $253.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: FactSet is a wide-moat, subscription-based financial data and analytics platform. 30.5% operating margins, 27% ROE, $621M FCF on an $8.9B market cap (~7% FCF yield), PEG 1.19, and analyst EPS revisions trending +1.2% higher. Revenue is sticky, recurring, and not economically sensitive in the same way as cyclicals. The stock has corrected ~43% from its 52w high of $442 to $250, creating a fair-price entry for a quality compounder. Technical: Currently at 24% of the 52w range (lower half — ideal Weinstein Stage 1/2 territory), with price just +0.4% above the 200-day SMA (recovering, not extended), SMA50 slope positive at +3.0%, and confirmed uptrend. No earnings until September 17 (73 days out), providing ample time for the thesis to play out without event risk. ATR-based stop at 1.5x gives a clean risk definition of ~7.6%.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below stop $231 (stop hit), (2) SMA50 turns negative for two consecutive weeks with price below SMA50 (trend break), (3) thesis deteriorates — subscriber churn acceleration, major client contract loss, or analyst EPS revisions turn sharply negative (-5%+ over 30 days), (4) position approaches September earnings with >20% open gain — consider trimming half to protect gains before binary event. Otherwise hold through earnings for position trade. Raise stop to breakeven once +8% gain achieved.
